6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffKit
7	
8	/-!
9	# The F5 kit at the `Zar` level: the forward map needs no global chart certificate
10	
11	`DivRepAffKit.lean` states the F5 forward machinery with a supplied *globally certified*
12	family on each carve chart (`divRepPullAt` takes
13	`CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g`).  But that family is used only through
14	`(DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar` — its certificate is consumed nowhere; the forward map is a
15	`DivFamZar.mapAlgHom` of a *class*.
16	
17	This file restates the kit with the input weakened to a `DivFamZar` class on each chart.
18	That matters for the DD-R endgame: the certificate lane's output is Zariski-local
19	(`IsLocallyCertified`, see `DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` / `DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`),
20	so a forward map demanding a global chart-ring certificate would have re-imposed exactly
21	the gate that was just removed.  With `divRepPullAtZar` it does not.
22	
23	The globally certified version is recovered by `divRepPullAtZar_toZar`, so this is a
24	weakening of the interface, not a second track.
25	
26	## Main declarations
27	
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullAtZar` — pull a supplied chart *class* to a test algebra.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullAtZar_toZar` — agreement with `divRepPullAt` on a globally
30	  certified chart family.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepChartFamilyZar.IsCompatible` — the choice-independence clause at
32	  the `Zar` level.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	set_option quotPrecheck false
37	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
38	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
39	
40	universe u
41	
42	open CategoryTheory
43	
44	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
45	
46	open Grassmannian Scheme
47	
48	section Curve
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
51	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
52	
53	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftDivRepAffKitZar :
54	    C.left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
55	
56	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
57	  [IsIntegral C.left]
58	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
59	  [QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
60	  [IsDominant pi]
61	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
62	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
63	variable [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0)]
64	  [Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)]
65	variable (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
66	variable (g : ℕ)
67	variable (r1 r2 : ℕ)
68	variable (b1 : Module.Basis (Fin r1) k
69	  ↥(divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
70	variable (b2 : Module.Basis (Fin r2) k
71	  ↥(divisorSections k
72	    ((windowM_choice pi hpi g + windowS_choice pi hpi g) • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))
73	
74	local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
75	  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
76	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
77	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
78	
79	local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
80	  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
81	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
82	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
83	
84	/-! ## F5 at the `Zar` level -/
85	
86	/-- Pull a supplied locally certified **class** on one carve chart to a test algebra.
87	This is `divRepPullAt` with the global chart certificate removed: the forward map only
88	ever transported a class, so a `DivFamZar` input suffices. -/
89	noncomputable def divRepPullAtZar
90	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
91	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
92	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
93	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
94	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
95	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (U i j)
96	
97	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
98	@[simp]
99	theorem divRepPullAtZar_id
100	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
101	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
102	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
103	    divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
104	      = U i j :=
105	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
106	
107	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
108	/-- Pulling a chart class through two algebra maps is pulling through the composite. -/
109	theorem divRepPullAtZar_comp
110	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
111	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
112	    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
113	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
114	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
115	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
116	      = divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
117	  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (U i j)).symm
118	
119	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
120	/-- **The interfaces agree.** On a globally certified chart family, the `Zar`-level
121	forward map is the old one — so this file weakens `DivRepAffKit`'s input rather than
122	introducing a parallel construction. -/
123	theorem divRepPullAtZar_toZar
124	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
125	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
126	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
127	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
128	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) :
129	    divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2
130	        (fun i j => (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar) i j omega
131	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega :=
132	  rfl
133	
134	namespace DivRepChartFamilyZar
135	
136	/-- The F5 overlap obligation at the `Zar` level: two chart points inducing the same
137	morphism to `DivScheme` pull the supplied classes to the same class. -/
138	def IsCompatible
139	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
140	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
141	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
142	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
143	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
144	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
145	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
146	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
147	      divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
148	        = divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'
149	
150	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
151	/-- Compatibility read at a morphism to `DivScheme`, the form the gluing consumes. -/
152	theorem eq_of_isCompatible
153	    {U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
154	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g}
155	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
156	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
157	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
158	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
159	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
160	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
161	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
162	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
163	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
164	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
165	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
166	    divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
167	      = divRepPullAtZar (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
168	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)
169	
170	end DivRepChartFamilyZar
171	
172	end Curve
173	
174	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# One fewer obligation on the affine pullback package (F6)
11	
12	`DivRepAffinePullback` (`Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean`) is the exact output F5 owes before the
13	affine representability equivalence is packaged.  As landed it demands FOUR fields:
14	`pull`, `pull_classify`, `isDivRepClassify_pull` and `pull_naturality`.
15	
16	The separation theorem (`Picard/DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean`) makes `pull_classify`
17	**redundant**: if the pulled class of every morphism satisfies the characterizing clause
18	for that morphism, then in particular `pull (classify F)` and `F` are both classified by
19	`classify F`, so they are equal.  This file records that.
20	
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pull_classify_of_isDivRepClassify_pull` — the reduction, stated for a
22	  bare `pull` function so it can be used before any package exists.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.ofPull` — **the three-field constructor**.  A
24	  producer now owes `pull`, the clause law, and naturality; the round-trip law is derived.
25	
26	This does not produce a `DivRepAffinePullback` — there is still no producer of one — but
27	it removes one of the four obligations from whoever writes it, and it is the obligation
28	that would otherwise have to be re-proved by a second cover chase.
29	-/

139	naturality. -/

/-- **`toZar` is injective**: both `DivFam` and `DivFamZar` are quotients by divisor
equality of the underlying local-equation systems, and `toZar` is induced by the
identity on representatives. -/
theorem DivFam.toZar_injective :
    Function.Injective (DivFam.toZar (C := C) (R := S) (π := π) (n := n)) := by
  intro F G h
  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
  | h F =>
    induction G using Quotient.inductionOn with
    | h G => exact DivFam.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr (DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mp h)

/-- **Step 1 — the certificate cover** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §2.1 step 1;
the carrier pattern inside `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`, made public): a
locally certified divisor class over `S` restricts, on a finite span-⊤ family of
basic opens, to classes of certified divisor families on the canonical
away-localizations. -/
theorem DivFamZar.exists_certified_away_rep (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (h : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range h) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ l : Fin m, ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (h l)) π n,
        (DivFam.mk G).toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg (Localization.Away (h l)) n F₀ := by
  obtain ⟨dp, hdp⟩ := Quotient.exists_rep F₀
  obtain ⟨m, h, hspan, hG⟩ := dp.2
  refine ⟨m, h, hspan, fun l => ?_⟩
  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C S (Localization.Away (h l))) :=
    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C S (Localization.Away (h l)) (h l)
  have hG' : ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (h l)) π n,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
        (dp.1.pullback (relCurveMap C S (Localization.Away (h l)))
          (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
            (relCurveMap C S (Localization.Away (h l))) dp.1)) := hG l
  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG'
  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩
  rw [← hdp]
  exact DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr hGdiv

if `F₁` over `S₁` and `F₂` over `S₂` both restrict the class `F₀` over `S`, their
`mapAlg`s to a common `k`/`S`-tower ring `B` agree — `toZar` is injective and
intertwines the total maps, and the Zar-level base change composes over towers. -/

    {S₁ : Type u} [CommRing S₁] [Algebra k S₁] [Algebra S S₁] [IsScalarTower k S S₁]
    {S₂ : Type u} [CommRing S₂] [Algebra k S₂] [Algebra S S₂] [IsScalarTower k S S₂]
    {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra S B] [IsScalarTower k S B]
    [Algebra S₁ B] [IsScalarTower k S₁ B] [IsScalarTower S S₁ B]
    [Algebra S₂ B] [IsScalarTower k S₂ B] [IsScalarTower S S₂ B]
    (F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n) (F₁ : DivFam C S₁ π n) (F₂ : DivFam C S₂ π n)
    (hZ₁ : F₁.toZar = DivFamZar.mapAlg S₁ n F₀)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarChartPair
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarVerdict

/-!
# Chart confinement: a divisor invariant, and an open condition on the base

`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean` proves the negative half of the certificate lane's gate: a certified
adaptation of a connected divisor confines that divisor to one pinned chart of `π`
(`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  This file supplies the two facts that turn that
no-go into a *decision* about the interface rather than an open question.

**1. The obstruction is about the divisor, not the presentation.**  `DivFamZar` is a `DivEq`
quotient, so a no-go stated about a local-equation system only bites the functor if it is
`DivEq`-invariant.  `DivEq.supportLocus_eq` proves it is: the unit locus is defined by germ
invertibility, and `DivEq` changes germs by units.  Hence
`not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`: no representative of the divisor
class admits a certified adaptation.  Re-spelling the equations cannot escape the obstruction.

**2. Confinement is an OPEN condition on the base.**  The support is closed and the relative
curve is proper over the test ring, so the set of base points whose support fibre lies in the
chart overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is open (`isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter`), and confinement at a
single fibre spreads to a Zariski neighbourhood
(`exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter`, the chart instance of the landed support tube).

Fact 2 is the licence the lane needs.  `IsLocallyCertified` — hence `DivFamZar` — is a
Zariski-local-on-the-base condition, and an *open* condition on the base may legitimately be
imposed by an atlas: the charts still cover.  So the repair of the interface is not "assume the
divisor avoids the vertical fibres" (a hypothesis on an arbitrary divisor, which
`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §Discipline (2) rightly forbids) but "the chart of the atlas records
which vertical fibres its divisors avoid" — legitimate exactly because the recorded condition
is open.  What Fact 2 does *not* supply, and what the repair still owes, is that these opens
COVER: with the two pinned charts fixed once and for all they provably do not
(`not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` applies to a connected divisor meeting both
vertical fibres over a base point, and no Zariski shrink separates the witnesses).

Finally `supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre` converts the global confinement hypothesis of
`forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` into the fibrewise one the seed geometry actually
produces, so the chart-shaped adaptation's clause (c1) can be discharged fibre by fibre.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq.unitLocus_eq` /
  `DivEq.supportLocus_eq` — the unit locus and the support locus are divisor invariants.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified` /
  `not_isCertified_of_not_isClosed_inter_chart₀` — the obstruction with NO connectivity

# The support of a pulled-back system is the preimage of the support

The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime,

`SupportTubeFinite.lean` proves one direction of the (c1) engine: a closed piece trace makes
the chart-local colength a finite `R`-module.  The converse was assumed throughout the
certificate lane — memory I-0209 states the Z-clopen principle as an "iff", and
`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` needs it to upgrade its verdict from "the assembler route is
unavailable" to "the certificate itself is unavailable" — but no declaration proved it.

It follows from the same triangle the forward direction uses, run backwards.  If
`Γ(X, V) ⧸ I` is a finite `R`-module then `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ Spec R` is a finite morphism,
hence universally closed; that morphism factors through `X`, and `X ⟶ Spec R` is separated, so
the first leg `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ X` is universally closed too
(`UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated`).  A universally closed morphism is a closed map,
so its range — which `range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec` identifies with the trace — is closed.

Consequences, both recorded here:

* the (c1)-finite clause of `IsCertified` is *equivalent* to leak-freeness at that piece, so
  the necessity results of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` and the verdict of
  `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` apply to `IsCertified` itself and not only to the assemblers;
* in particular a **certified** adaptation of a connected divisor forces that divisor inside a
  single pinned chart of `pi`.  `DivFamZar` is therefore blind to connected divisors meeting
  both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — over any base, after any Zariski shrink, for any adaptation.

### 3. Two admissible repairs, and one that does not work

**R1 — vary the P¹ coordinate.** Every declaration in the chain is generic in `π`, constrained
only by `[IsFinite π]` / `[IsAffineHom π]` (+ `[IsDominant π]`) and
`hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)` (`DivSchemeSeedUnivFields.lean:58`). So
replacing `π` by `γ ∘ π` for `γ ∈ Aut(P¹_k)` costs NOTHING in the landed material: every lemma
applies verbatim to the twisted map, and the twisted charts `π⁻¹(P¹ ∖ {c})` are affine because
`π` is affine. `IsLocallyCertified` (and the atlas) then quantify over `γ` as well as over the
base cover. COST, and it is the reason this is not free: **`Aut(P¹)` does not exist in this
project.** `P1 k` is a `Proj` (`Curve/P1.lean:135`) with `chartOpen : Fin 2 → Opens` (:200) and
no `PGL₂` action anywhere. R1 owes the `GL₂(k)`-action on `Proj (k[X₀,X₁])` and transitivity on
`P¹(k)`.

**R2 — generalize `FinCoverData` to σ-charts.** For `σ ∈ H⁰(bΘ)` let `U_σ` be its
non-vanishing locus; `V₀` and `V₁` are the cases `σ = t₀ᵇ`, `t₁ᵇ`. A divisor avoiding `Z(σ)` is
swallowed by the single piece `U_σ`. This stays inside the existing `relThetaSections`
vocabulary, but owes affineness of `U_σ` (complement of an ample divisor) and a wide refactor
of `FinCoverData`/`DivisorAdaptation`/`chartProd`.

**REJECTED — delete clause (c1) from `IsCertified`.** Tempting, because `Module.Flat R
(colength j)` is free from fibrewise regularity alone
(`flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField`, `SupportTube.lean:313` — no finiteness, no
no-leak), while `Module.Finite` is exactly the culprit. But the (c2)/(c3)/(c4) keystones
(`SlicingFlatKernel.lean`, variable block at :221-224) all carry `[Module.Finite R M]` with
`M = chartProd`, which IS finite colengths. Dropping (c1) leaves `projective_glued`,
`rankAtStalk_glued` and both flat-cokernel clauses with no landed route. Do not re-propose this
without first supplying a finiteness-free replacement for `SlicingFlatKernel`.

### 4. Why a repair of this shape is legitimate at all

§Discipline (2) forbids a support-separation hypothesis, and it is right to: assuming
`supp D ∩ π⁻¹({0,∞}) = ∅` about an arbitrary divisor assumes the conclusion. The repair does
something different — the ATLAS RECORDS which vertical fibres its divisors avoid — and that is
legitimate because the recorded condition is **open on the base**. New this round,
kernel-checked (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean`):

* `isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter` — the base points whose support fibre lies in
  `V₀ ⊓ V₁` form an OPEN subset of `Spec R`;
* `exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter` — confinement at one fibre spreads to a
  Zariski neighbourhood (the chart instance of the landed support tube);
* `supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre` — fibrewise confinement at every base point IS the
  global hypothesis `forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` wants.

So a chart of the atlas may carve by avoidance without losing points. What the repair still
owes is that the carved opens **cover** — and with the two pinned charts fixed once and for all
they provably do not (§1(c)). Covering is exactly what R1/R2 buy.

### 5. The covering obligation, stated

For a relative divisor whose support is finite over `Spec R`, and any `s ∈ Spec R`: the fibre
`D_s` is finite, so `π(D_s)` is a finite subset of `P¹` over `κ(s)`; if `k` is infinite,
`P¹(k)` is infinite, so two distinct `c₀, c₁ ∈ P¹(k)` avoid `π(D_s)`; `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R`
is proper (`instIsProperRelCurveHom`, `SupportTube.lean:194`), hence closed, so the image of
`supportLocus ∩ π⁻¹({c₀,c₁})` is closed and misses `s`; over the open complement the divisor is
confined to `π⁻¹(P¹ ∖ {c₀,c₁})`, i.e. to `V₀ ⊓ V₁` for the `γ`-twist carrying `{c₀,c₁}` to

`forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`) give
clause (c1) FREE, with no fibre, no tube and no idempotent.

Two hypotheses to watch. (i) **`k` infinite.** `Challenge.lean` states the Jacobian over an
arbitrary field; a finite-field route needs `|P¹(k)| > deg D`, i.e. a base change to `k(T)` or
a degree-`d` point, and must be scheduled, not assumed. (ii) **Finiteness of the support over
the base** must come from the seed's own degree data, NOT from the certificate — otherwise the

`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivGen.lean:283`, `side := (exists_seedPoint …).choose`; `seedUniv'`,

`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivPointwise.lean:88`), so a point of `π⁻¹(∞)` is legal everywhere.

**(b) ADDENDUM 2 §4's "tractable half" is not a half, and its argument is circular.**
Θ = `fiberWeilDivisor π` is supported on `V₀ ∖ V₁` (`RiemannRoch/FLVFiberToolkit.lean:292`,
:311, :254), i.e. set-theoretically **Θ = V₁ᶜ**. So "`supportLocus ∩ π⁻¹(∞) = ∅`" IS the
disjunct `supportLocus ⊆ V₁` of the verdict — a whole side of the conclusion, not a tractable
half of it. And the route is circular: `IsGenerator.dvd` forces `eqn z` to generate `K·𝒪` on
its piece, so `supportLocus` is the base locus of `K`, and "a generator of exact pole order `a`
exists at `y ∈ Θ`" holds iff the base locus misses `y`. Premise = conclusion.

**(c) There is an explicit counterexample, and no Zariski shrink of the base evades it.**
Over `k[t]`, on `C = P¹`, `π = id`, take the degree-2 form

  `F = t·X² + X·Y + t·Y²`,   `D = Z(F) ⊆ P¹ × A¹_t`.

The coefficients `(t, 1, t)` generate the unit ideal, so `D` is a relative effective Cartier
divisor, finite flat of degree 2. `F(1,0) = F(0,1) = t`, so the fibre `D₀ = Z(XY) = {0, ∞}`

coprime coefficients, hence irreducible in `k[x,t]`; the only point over `Y = 0` is `(∞, 0)`,
which lies in the closure (`t = -x/(x²+1) → 0` as `x → ∞`). So `D` is IRREDUCIBLE. `D → A¹_t`
is finite surjective, so over every nonempty open `U ⊆ Spec k[t]`, `D_U` is a nonempty open of
an irreducible space, hence irreducible, hence preconnected. Every Zariski cover of `Spec k[t]`
has a member containing `t = 0`, and over that member `D` is connected and meets both vertical
fibres. By `supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:131`)

localization cannot help" with `Spec R[x]/(x²−t)` over `R = k[t]`. That divisor's points are

witness. The conclusion stands; the witness above is the correct one.

kernel-checked: `Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq.supportLocus_eq`
(`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean`) — the support locus is a `DivEq` invariant, because the
unit locus is a germ-invertibility locus and `DivEq` only rescales germs by units. Hence
`not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`: **no representative** of the class
admits a certified adaptation. `DivFamZar` is a `DivEq` quotient, so this closes the last
escape hatch. `DivFamZar` is not the relative-divisor functor, and `divRep` stated against it
represents the wrong object.

### 2. The binding constraint is `FinCoverData`, not `π`, not the cover, not `L`, not the base

`FinCoverData` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:160-176`) hardwires `h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(V₀)`,
`h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(V₁)` with a partition of unity on EACH pinned chart; `pieces` (:186) are
therefore basic opens of `V₀`/`V₁`, and they cover the whole curve. Clause (c1)-finiteness IS
leak-freeness (`supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength`, `DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:123`), so
every piece trace is clopen in the support; a connected support then lies in one piece, hence
in one pinned chart. Consequently:

* refining the cover cannot help (more pieces, same union of traces);
* shrinking the base cannot help (it re-states the condition, and does not disconnect);
* a cleverer submodule `L` cannot help (the `L`-free form is already the general one);
* re-spelling the equations cannot help (§1(d)).

Any repair must introduce an adaptation piece that is **not contained in a single pinned
chart**. That is the whole content of the decision.

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model typically suffices. The
  Horizon agent chooses the model and effort at dispatch time; do not encode that
  spend policy in `config.yaml` or the descriptor.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)

250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]

307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))

330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
331	
332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
336	
337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
340	DEFINITION. -/
341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
346	
347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
350	
351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
356	    (by
357	      intro a ha
358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442

450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns

460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)

481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :

484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)

488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)

69	/-- **A surjection of finite projective modules of equal rank at every stalk is
70	injective** (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3 item 5, the equality mechanism): the projective
71	lifting splits the surjection, so the kernel is a finite projective direct summand
72	whose rank at every stalk is zero — a subsingleton, by
73	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton`. -/
74	theorem LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq
75	    {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R M] [Module R N]
76	    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Projective R M] [Module.Projective R N]
77	    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
78	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
79	      Module.rankAtStalk M p = Module.rankAtStalk N p) :
80	    Function.Injective φ := by
81	  -- a right inverse of `φ` (the projective lifting), and the induced splitting
82	  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := φ.exists_rightInverse_of_surjective (LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hsurj)
83	  obtain ⟨e, he₁, -⟩ := (LinearMap.exact_subtype_ker_map φ).splitSurjectiveEquiv
84	    (Submodule.injective_subtype (LinearMap.ker φ)) ⟨l, hl⟩
85	  -- the kernel is a finite projective direct summand
86	  haveI : Module.Finite R N := Module.Finite.of_surjective φ hsurj
87	  haveI : Module.Finite R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
88	    Module.Finite.of_surjective
89	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
90	      (Prod.fst_surjective.comp e.surjective)
91	  haveI : Module.Projective R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
92	    Module.Projective.of_split (LinearMap.ker φ).subtype
93	      (LinearMap.fst R ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
94	      (LinearMap.ext fun x => by
95	        have hx := LinearMap.congr_fun he₁ x
96	        simp only [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, Function.comp_apply] at hx ⊢
97	        rw [hx, e.apply_symm_apply]
98	        rfl)
99	  -- the kernel has rank zero at every stalk
100	  have hker : Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) = 0 := by
101	    funext p
102	    have h1 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv e) p
103	    have h2 := congrFun (Module.rankAtStalk_prod (R := R) ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) N) p
104	    rw [Pi.add_apply] at h2
105	    have h3 := hrank p
106	    rw [Pi.zero_apply]
107	    omega
108	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(LinearMap.ker φ) :=
109	    Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton.mp hker
110	  exact LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mp (Submodule.eq_bot_of_subsingleton)
111	
112	/-- **Nested submodules with same-rank finite projective quotients are equal**: the
113	canonical surjection `M ⧸ K₁ → M ⧸ K₂` is injective by the rank engine, so the larger
114	submodule collapses onto the smaller. -/
115	theorem Submodule.eq_of_le_of_rankAtStalk_quotient_eq
116	    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {K₁ K₂ : Submodule R M} (hle : K₁ ≤ K₂)
117	    [Module.Finite R (M ⧸ K₁)] [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₁)]
118	    [Module.Projective R (M ⧸ K₂)]
119	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
120	      Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₁) p = Module.rankAtStalk (M ⧸ K₂) p) :
121	    K₁ = K₂ := by
122	  have hcomap : K₁ ≤ K₂.comap LinearMap.id := hle
123	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap) := by
124	    intro y
125	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.mkQ_surjective K₂ y
126	    exact ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk x, rfl⟩
127	  have hinj := LinearMap.injective_of_surjective_of_rankAtStalk_eq _ hsurj hrank
128	  refine le_antisymm hle fun x hx => ?_
129	  have h0 : Submodule.mapQ K₁ K₂ LinearMap.id hcomap (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) = 0 := by
130	    rw [Submodule.mapQ_apply, LinearMap.id_apply]
131	    exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₂).mpr hx
132	  have hx0 : (Submodule.Quotient.mk x : M ⧸ K₁) = 0 := hinj (by rw [h0, map_zero])
133	  exact (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero K₁).mp hx0
134	
135	end RankEngine

123	/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family on every carve chart:
124	two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled locally
125	certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this from
126	its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
127	def IsCompatible
128	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
129	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
130	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
131	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
132	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
133	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
134	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
135	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
136	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
137	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'

142	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
143	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
144	      CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
145	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
146	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
147	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
148	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
149	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
150	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
151	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
152	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
153	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
154	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
155	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
156	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
157	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
158	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)

163	
164	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
165	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
166	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
167	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
168	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
169	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
170	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
171	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
172	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
173	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
174	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
175	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
176	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
177	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
178	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)

182	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
183	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
184	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
185	noncomputable def equiv
186	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
187	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
188	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
189	  toFun := D.pull S
190	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
191	  left_inv v :=
192	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
193	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
194	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S

198	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
199	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
200	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
201	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=

209	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
210	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=

214	theorem equiv_naturality
215	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
216	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
217	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
218	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
219	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
220	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)

222	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
